The Dispatch · Issue 1 · 26 November 2026

The Grass Bank is open

Our first Dispatch: what's on the site, and where to start.

The Grass Bank is open.

If you signed up when we were called Cricket Times: same journal, same cricket, new name.

The Grass Bank is written for the fans of the game. Those who sit on the grass banks at numerous grounds around the world watching Test cricket, or for that matter under-15 cricket, simply because they love the game. They watch because it is fun. They can dress however they want, they can be from any country around the world, they can sing their own songs or no songs at all, they can support their own players or any player, and they can heckle, but with humour, not malice. Some may bring scorecards and follow the game ball by ball; others may bring canvas and easel and paint the ground. They are all fans of this beautiful game, and our writing is for them.

What's on the site

Free for everyone

  • Articles on the home page, with audio for some of them.
  • Players: every Test cricketer, each with their own page.
  • Scorecards.
  • Fixtures: every Test coming up.
  • The WTC race: who can still reach the final.

Free with an account

  • Yorker, our monthly quiz, and its leaderboard. The top five each month earn a crown.
  • The Coffee shop debate: comments under every article.

For subscribers

  • The stats pages: batting, bowling, captaincy, keeping and countries, back to 1877.
  • Compare: put any players side by side, across eras.
  • Simulations: replay a Test, or pick an XI from any era.
  • The full archive, the audio library and Behind the Scenes.

The annual plan gets cheaper every season you stay. The first 100 subscribers go on our Honours Board. Be one of them.

What we've been writing

Cape Town

The Spirit of Cricket

Eight years after Cape Town, some of the men in that dressing room are telling a different story. Cricket owes its fans the truth.

Three bad boys!

Bancroft, Warner and Smith took the blame for Cape Town. Was that the whole story?

The numbers

Is a century equivalent to a 5 wicket haul?

They’re treated as equal career milestones. They’re not even close: a five-wicket haul is worth close to 140 runs.

Introducing AvRate

Average or strike rate? The greats need both. One number that adds them up.

AvRate, part two: what does a wicket cost?

We turned AvRate round for bowlers. The question is simple: what did each wicket cost you?

Do captains get it right?

Hussain at the Gabba, Ponting at Edgbaston, Rohit at the Oval. We replayed three famous toss calls to see what they really cost.

The arguments and the stories

No more GOAT, only GILT

How can we call anyone the greatest of all time when we never saw most of them play? A better question to ask.

If we now call batsmen batters, what about 12th man, third man and night watchman?

Once batsmen became batters, the rest of the scorecard started to look nervous.
